cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's machine review HANGS General Contracting's quarter. A review is lighter than an audit.
Analytical procedures compare the quarter with the last one and the budget. Revenue is up 13%, but the margin fell.
The controller answers every question in writing. One customer shares the same owners.
Now it rebuilds each job's revenue, and it ties to the books. But $259,200 comes from a change the customer has not signed.
Interest is booked only when paid, so $35,350 is missing. The loan covenants, promises made to the bank, are met, but net worth has only about $130,000 to spare.
Last, it weighs what it found against materiality and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. Interest expense is $6,685 short, well under materiality. The bigger question is the unsigned change, which also decides whether net worth still meets the covenant. Ten items stay open. This is not a review report: the CPA, a person, concludes and signs.
